correspondence.component_scope: Chosen highland opening and southwest-then-south headward passage.
correspondence.finding: The upper original shows the selected opening on sparsely vegetated mountain terrain and its descending drainage hollow into the greener enclosed valley. Parts 1–3 follow the same receiving hollow and valley as they bend southwest and south. Local clouds lie mainly beside this passage; the geographic trough and continuation remain readable. No lake or glacier crossing is required, and no precise name is imposed on the opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper valley bends and tributary receiving settings.
correspondence.finding: The selection turns west within a continuous vegetated valley, with adjoining steep ridges and tributary hollows, then makes the southern and northwestern bends. The upper original and overview expose the full ordinary valley connection through all seven stored parts. Small generalized offsets and sparse clouds do not establish a separate-basin transfer. The report places Chacchan on the upper main-course sequence and distinguishes Pira and Vado as contributing tributaries; it is not used to rename all adjacent streams.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle westward corridor and broad cultivated receiving area.
correspondence.finding: The images show a continuous incised-to-cultivated valley through the westward parts and the northwestern swing, including the broad receiving junction before the lower entrenched bends. The 2007 study calls its middle main course Grande and places the Yaután contribution before the lower Casma naming scope. Precise reach-name transition points are not digitized from the prose.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower southern bend and northwestward approach to the coastal plain.
correspondence.finding: A wide continuous irrigated valley curves southwest, west and northwest between dry hills. All selected parts remain within this connected valley and receiving floor; fields, channel belts, roads and tributary fans are visible. The corridor then opens toward the larger coastal settlement and tributary join. This is ordinary geographic correspondence and does not depend on a presently wet individual thread.

correspondence.component_scope: Final cultivated plain, drainage outlets and Pacific shore.
correspondence.finding: The lower original shows the selected continuation through the broad cultivated coastal receiving floor to the Pacific coast. The generalized final path crosses this shared floor rather than following every visible channel bend. The shore, lower drainage channels and common receiving coast are continuously exposed; no separate enclosed basin or missing lake-to-feeder transfer appears.

correspondence.component_scope: Original-source terminal setting, retained independently of the rendered end.
correspondence.finding: The stored source endpoint falls in Pacific coastal water just off the cultivated lower Casma shore, near the southern side of the exposed lower drainage-outlet setting. It is evaluated as the receiving sea setting, not moved to the current visible channel mouth or shore edge.

correspondence.component_scope: Rendered terminal setting, retained independently of the original-source end.
correspondence.finding: The distinct rendered endpoint is slightly northwest of the stored source endpoint in the same nearshore Pacific receiving water. The final rendered segment and endpoint are kept as supplied. Image scale does not justify an exact tidal edge, bank or active outfall claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern southern-branch opening
correspondence.finding: The selected eastern opening follows a narrow westward drainage corridor through low wooded and wetland terrain. Its bends and receiving passage remain continuous across the eastern photographic panel; the selection is not extended to a different headwater.
correspondence.scope_limit: No separate opening name, exact bank or currently wet thread is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern branch through lowland bends
correspondence.finding: The southern channel and its adjoining wetland valley continue west, bending through several broad lowland curves and receiving small lateral drainages. Imagery exposes the interval hidden under the CEHQ station panel.
correspondence.scope_limit: The station081101 annotation masks part of the original regional map; the missing cartographic interval is supplied by independent imagery.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern branch joins the northern receiving river
correspondence.finding: The selected southern branch turns northwest through a common low valley to the junction with the separately retained northern tributary fragment. The CEHQ original places Rivière Machisakahikanistikw along the southern branch and Rivière Pontax on the northern river that continues into the shared lower corridor.
correspondence.scope_limit: The separately named southern branch is not an alias of Pontax.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern tributary opening and westward river
correspondence.finding: The selected northern opening is already in a visible river channel. It winds west and southwest through rocky wooded terrain and broadens toward the receiving valley; both stored opening parts have ordinary continuous correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern river bends and lateral joins
correspondence.finding: The northern river makes westward and southwestward bends through the same connected channel-and-valley system, passing small lateral drainage joins. CEHQ places the Pontax name along this northern branch.

correspondence.component_scope: Tributary source/render confluence ending
correspondence.finding: The last retained tributary part reaches the shared junction with the mainstem southern branch. Its stored source and rendered endpoints coincide at that confluence; neither is the marine mouth.
correspondence.scope_limit: The role and ending remain distinct from the mainstem sea terminal.

correspondence.component_scope: Shared lower receiving corridor
correspondence.finding: Below the two-fragment join, the broader river winds northwest and west through a continuous wooded/wetland lowland. Bends, small side joins and the widening coastal approach are readable in the western photographic panel and the regional map. The named Pontax branch continues through this receiving system.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower river and bay-mouth setting
correspondence.finding: The lower river turns west through a sediment-lined mouth with bars and broad tidal-flat surroundings on the east side of James Bay. The photographs separate it from the larger neighboring outlet to the south.
correspondence.scope_limit: Neither tidal state nor the exact active mouth branch is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Separate mainstem source sea endpoint
correspondence.finding: The stored source endpoint occupies the river-mouth/channel and sediment-flat receiving setting. It remains separately recorded from the rendered endpoint and from the tributary confluence.

correspondence.component_scope: Separate mainstem rendered sea endpoint
correspondence.finding: The rendered endpoint lies slightly southeast within the same coastal-mouth setting. The two terminal locations have ordinary shared river-to-bay correspondence without collapsing or moving them.
correspondence.scope_limit: No surveyed shoreline or present flow-state assertion.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen short eastward opening and its proposed turn north into the southern wetland
correspondence.finding: The selection begins in a forested and partly cleared tract near the Transcametá road. The municipal sheet shows nearby streams and a wetland corridor but no supported transfer for this opening. Original imagery shows the forest/road/clearing setting and nearby wetland; it does not sufficiently establish the selected opening-to-wetland connection. This is a concrete receiving-link gap, not a demand for an exact bank, visible current water thread or culvert-operation evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward southern wetland corridor after the opening gap
correspondence.finding: The municipal southern sheet and imagery agree on the elongated low wetland corridor with branch traces, vegetated patches and ordinary receiving connections within that corridor. The route can be followed through this common wetland setting without requiring a single visible blue/wet thread throughout. No individual pool, river name, regulated reservoir or present-flow direction is assigned. The first portion of part2 and final portion of part10 are bounded by the separate connector limits.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastern departure from the elongated wetland across the Transcametá strip toward the eastern river
correspondence.finding: The selected route turns east from the wetland toward the separately mapped Anavera corridor. The sources depict both receiving settings but do not establish their selected cross-connection through the intervening vegetated/road strip. The imagery shows wooded ground and adjacent drainage traces without sufficient continuous geographic evidence for that transfer. No separate basin or impossible connection is inferred merely from the image.

correspondence.component_scope: Mapped eastern river corridor and north-to-west bend toward the larger receiving river
correspondence.finding: The first-sheet river labelled RIO ANAVERA follows the same general northward corridor and westward bending reach as the selected middle route. Its connection with the separately named Rio Caracuru setting and northward continuation are mapped. The exact printed label is retained as a bounded middle-reach observation; FAPESPA spells a corresponding eastern tributary Anauerá, but that spelling is not promoted to a whole-selection alias.

correspondence.component_scope: Agro-Oeste/Vila Boa Vista setting, channel widening, Ilha das Flores and Rio Oeiras join
correspondence.finding: The maps depict a connected receiving river past Agro-Oeste and Vila Boa Vista, broadening around Ilha das Flores and receiving the separately named Rio Oeiras from the west. Portel directly labels the lower course Rio Araticu. These joins are ordinary mapped river/floodplain correspondence; exact banks and contemporary tidal flow or management operation are not required or claimed. Caracuru and Oeiras remain distinct tributary/reach names rather than aliases.

correspondence.component_scope: Stage2 lower estuarine Araticu past Oeiras do Pará to the actual selected ending
correspondence.finding: The second fragment remains in the continuous broad lower Rio Araticu corridor past Oeiras do Pará and beside the Ilha Grande/Furo do Oeiras setting. Both the stored source endpoint and the rendered endpoint lie within that lower river setting north of town. They remain before the farther northern opening into Rio Pará; no route to that mouth or the open ocean is appended. The supplied sea class is retained as metadata only. The side furo and receiving Pará are not whole-selection river aliases.

terminal_description.source_endpoint: Within the broad lower Araticu north of Oeiras do Pará, before the farther Rio Pará opening.
terminal_description.render_endpoint: Within the same broad lower river setting; not substituted for or treated as identical to the source endpoint.

bounded_receiving_system_candidate.name: Rio Araticu
bounded_receiving_system_candidate.scope: Mapped middle/lower receiving river and actual terminal setting only. It is not a completed representative for the whole selected composite until the two upper connector limits are resolved.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern feeder opening and southward receiving channel
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening lies in a narrow southwesterly feeder valley that joins the larger southward incised drainage. The upper clean-pixel panel and closer local opening crop expose that ordinary connection through the rocky terrain.
correspondence.scope_limit: The selected opening is retained without extension to another headwater; nearby ponds are not all asserted to be serial through-flow lakes.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper valley bends and lateral joins
correspondence.finding: The receiving corridor bends southeast and then south between low ridges, receiving lateral ravines and passing a small broadened-water section. The original shows a continuous valley/river setting despite generalized selected-line offsets.
correspondence.scope_limit: This is ordinary valley correspondence, not a surveyed centerline or exact current wet thread.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper large-lake passage and southern outlet
correspondence.finding: The selected upper valley reaches the northern side of a large elongated inland lake. The lake extends south and narrows through a short outlet passage into the next lake-rich valley. The whole lake and both approach/outlet settings are visible in overlapping northern and middle original-pixel panels.
correspondence.scope_limit: The waterbody has no independently established proper name in the inspected source.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern lake chain to the western pond and river
correspondence.finding: The next elongated waterbody narrows toward its western side. A short low connecting passage links that western lake margin to the smaller pond immediately west, which opens south into a clearly visible river. A closer crop of the same successfully acquired original exposes this local receiving connection.
correspondence.scope_limit: An additional source request was unnecessary once the local original-pixel crop established ordinary connected lake/valley terrain. No current discharge or exact active channel is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle river, small lakes and tributary joins
correspondence.finding: The river proceeds south through several small lake-like widenings, bends west around rocky ground and returns southeast into a common receiving valley. Eastern side-valleys and waterbodies join this corridor, while larger lakes farther west remain separate contextual features.
correspondence.scope_limit: The finding does not assign one river name to the individual lake passages or tributaries.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower southward valley and broadened-water reaches
correspondence.finding: The selected route follows a southward river valley, passes broadened water and shallow alluvial reaches, then bends southeast toward the lower lake/inlet approach. Overlapping middle and southern panels cover the interval.
correspondence.scope_limit: Scattered clouds and image-mosaic boundaries limit fine channel detail but do not interrupt ordinary receiving-valley correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower lake-like coastal reach and outlet approach
correspondence.finding: The lower waterway occupies a long confined water-filled valley beside rocky slopes. Its eastern margin and southern continuation are visible alongside a darker mosaic patch. The corridor opens into a sediment-rich mouth and the head of a larger marine inlet.
correspondence.scope_limit: The source does not establish exact tidal limits or whether every broadened lower water section is classified as a lake, river or inlet; ordinary connected geography is sufficient.

correspondence.component_scope: Stored source sea endpoint at the inlet head
correspondence.finding: The stored source terminal is in the sediment-lined upper marine receiving setting where the river/valley opens into the inlet. Its local position is distinct from the much farther south rendered ending.
correspondence.scope_limit: The sea classification is retained from the supplied metadata; no new legal shoreline or tidal boundary is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Separate rendered extension and marine endpoint
correspondence.finding: The final rendered part continues far south to the outer marine receiving water. Its generalized straight segment crosses the inlet-side land margin instead of tracing every bend of the open water; the photographed inlet independently supplies the continuous coastal receiving connection around those projections. The rendered endpoint is in the outer marine water.
correspondence.scope_limit: This terminal extension is not asserted to be a natural river channel, and it is not renamed or moved. Source and rendered endings remain separate; no geometry correction or revalidation occurred.

Front matter and contents were consulted to bound the volume; no name or inland/terminal correspondence was adopted from it. No ARC401 or held chart substitute was requested.
